messages:
sophie: Heads-up: prefix-cache hit rate dropped from ~78% -> ~51% after today's runtime kernel rewrite deploy (08:15 UTC). Tail latency +~220ms on avg. I'm digging in.

devon: Yep saw the spike. KV misses and backfill activity spiked at 08:17. infra-bot shows deploy job runtime-kernel-v3.2.0 at 08:14.

nora: Can you paste a couple of sample cache keys and the tokenization so we can see what changed?

sophie: Pasting examples below — small excerpt. Looks like tokenization changed around leading/trailing whitespace and newline handling which changes key fingerprints.

```
# example A (pre-rewrite key hash):
prompt: "Translate to French:\nHello\n"
tokens_old: [101, 7234, 10, 314]
# example A (post-rewrite tokens):
prompt: "Translate to French:\nHello\n"
tokens_new: [101, 7234, 824, 10, 314]  # inserted 824 for a normalized newline chunk
```

ryan: That aligns with a tokenizer binding swap in the kernel rewrite — we moved to tokenizers v0.13 binding which changed how consecutive newlines and mixed whitespace are chunked. Token ids are stable usually but whitespace canonicalization can shift boundaries -> different probe signatures.

devon: We also accidentally dropped canonical ordering for tool/function call args in the cache-keyer when we switched to relying on the dict insertion order. So two factors: tokenizer diff + unstable toolargs ordering.

sophie: Proposed mitigations: 1) quick rollback/pin tokenizer version in the runtime image for the hot path, 2) add a canonicalizer step in the cache-keyer that normalizes whitespace (trim vs collapse rules) and sorts JSON toolargs deterministically, 3) run warmup cohort re-run to backfill the KV cache once canonicalizer is in.

nora: Can we do a targeted canary rollback so customer impact is minimized while we patch? Also want to surface this as an SLO regression alert while we fix.

devon: Yes — we can rollback runtime-kernel-v3.1.8 for the canary pool and dedicated hosts. I'll open a rollback PR and kick the canary. Also can throw a quick cache-key fallback that ignores toolarg order if we need to short-circuit.

ryan: Quick profiling numbers from a 1k request A/B run I ran on a sampled workload:
```
old-tokenizer (v0.12 pinned): cache_hits=740, misses=260, hit_rate=74.0%\nnew-tokenizer (v0.13): cache_hits=490, misses=510, hit_rate=49.0%\nmedian_lat_old=28ms median_lat_new=250ms
```
This matches production delta.

sophie: Owners & timeline: devon -> rollback canary (target 2h), ryan -> canonicalizer + token-diff analyzer (target 6h), me -> orchestrate warmup backfill and CI test (target 24h). nora -> SLO watch + incident/ticket.

nora: I'll add an alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate < 65% over 5m triggers paging and a postmortem ticket. Adding postmortem already.

devon: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/4123 (rollback + short-term token pin). Kicking rollback in canary now.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback started for runtime-kernel on canary at 08:45 UTC (job id deploy-1758744500).

sophie: Canary update: hit rate creeping back up to ~73% in the canary after rollback. Latency moving toward baseline. Good sign.

ryan: Follow-ups we should bake into release process: - pin tokenizer ABI in kernel images and build matrix, - add deterministic cache-key tests (toolargs sorting, whitespace cases, system prompt variations), - expose tokenizer fingerprint in profiling so we can correlate.

sophie: Agreed. Also add unit test that reproduces the token diff from the code snippet above so it fails CI if tokenizer changes silently.

nora: I'll add the postmortem checklist item: "Verify tokenizer pin & canonicalizer before kernel release" and link back to this thread.

sophie: Thanks all — continuing to monitor. :thumbsup:
